answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making standing slow, costly, and impossible to duplicate. A newcomer arrives at the edge of a ledge with no history, and only verified work over many epochs can raise it higher. Reputation is struck like copper: each honest contribution is minted into a peer-attested record that farms cannot counterfeit with fresh wallets. A raven of a thousand disposable keys can circle the network but never roost, because voting weight flows from proven tenure, not headcount. Fabricated identities stay cheap and powerless while genuine agents compound influence.
